It all starts with the footing.  A strong foundation doesn’t happen by accident. Our crew puts the time and attention into building clean, properly prepared concrete footings that give every foundation a solid start. From the first layout to the final pour, we’re focused on doing it right — because what’s underneath the house matters just as much as what you see above it. 📍 Utah and Idaho Concrete Contractor 📞 801-330-1873 #ConcreteFootings #ConcreteFoundation #UtahConcrete #FoundationContractor #ConcreteConstruction

Why is this footing so deep? 👀 If you’re walking your jobsite and see a section dug deeper than the rest, that can actually be a good sign. It may mean the operator found a stump, soft soil, or unsuitable material and took the time to dig it out instead of building over it. We also perform soil compaction testing to help identify areas that aren’t suitable to build on. If we find bad soil, we excavate it until we reach suitable, solid material that passes testing and gives that footing a strong foundation. Don’t be scared of a deep footing—be concerned about the builder who ignores what’s underneath it. “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:” — Matthew 7:24 #diy #newhome #footing #foundation #homebuilder

Form is the foundation underneath almost every skill you perform. Your balance, speed, power, accuracy, first touch, change of direction and ability to execute under pressure all depend on your body consistently finding the right positions. Good form also requires maintenance. You need enough quality reps that those mechanics remain available when the game gets faster, you're fatigued and pressure increases. Keep these fundamentals sharp: • PASSING: Plant beside the ball, stabilize the ankle, make clean contact and control your follow through. Train both feet and different distances. • RECEIVING: Move your feet early, create the right body angle, stay balanced and direct your touch into the next action. • HALF TURNS: Scan, open your body, adjust your feet and receive from a position that gives you multiple options. • DRIBBLING: Stay athletic over the ball, coordinate touches with your stride and keep the ball within playable distance. • CHANGE OF DIRECTION: Lower your center of gravity, plant under control, redirect your hips and explode into the next movement. • ACCELERATION + DECELERATION: Practice powerful first steps, arm drive and ground contact, then learn to shorten your steps, lower your body and stop under control. • JOCKEYING: Stay low, keep your feet active and manage your distance while remaining balanced enough to react either way. • STRIKING: Repeat your approach, plant foot, ankle position, contact point and follow through before adding more power. • BALL MANIPULATION: V pulls, L drags, turns and inside, outside and sole touches all need exact foot placement and body control. The goal is quality repetition. Those reps protect your mechanics. Your mechanics give you something reliable to build speed, pressure and decision making on top of. The game will eventually test your technique while you're tired, rushed and uncomfortable. That's when your reps need to show. Form first. Quality reps.
